cards.title: Being a Working Parent: School Holidays Nightmare
cards.body: Working parents face constant logistical challenges balancing work and school schedules. Emily Mulligan argues school holidays should be a time families look forward to, not dread due to childcare and work conflicts.

cards.title: Halloween Magic: Ditching Cynicism for Family Connection
cards.body: Iman Amrani embraces Halloween celebrations as meaningful autumn traditions with roots in Day of the Dead and Samhain. She's choosing to create moments of magic and connection with her children rather than dismiss the holiday.

cards.title: When Good Parents Have Something to Regret
cards.body: Parents can acknowledge that loving intentions may cause unintended pain to their children. Recognition of regrets transforms into empathy without self-condemnation.

cards.title: Talking to Kids About Politics
cards.body: With political events front and center, parents should consider how and whether to discuss politics with their children. Open conversations help kids develop critical thinking about current events.

cards.title: Don't Create a Monster: Curating Accountability
cards.body: Parents want children to be accountable, resilient, and successful. Mistaking sympathy for empathy prevents kids from developing these essential qualities.

cards.title: Why Gen Z Doesn't Answer the Phone
cards.body: Phone calls trigger anxiety in Gen Z, who experience them very differently than older generations. Understanding this generational difference helps parents find communication compromises.

cards.title: Gaslighting in Parent-Child Relationships
cards.body: Recent research examines gaslighting in parent-child dynamics and its link to depression and self-blame in youth. Understanding these patterns helps parents recognize harmful communication patterns.
